author: Codex socialist_green assessment agent (AI-assisted independent assessment)
changeNote: Completed 240 individually interpreted responses and separate substantive evidence review. User authorised neutral representative doctrinal modelling; no 12Axes answers or scores imported.

metadata.name: Democratic Socialism (DSA programme tradition)
metadata.description: The contemporary DSA variant seeking a democratic socialist republic, social ownership, universal provision and expanded workplace democracy.
metadata.period: Contemporary United States; live DSA programme at 4 October 2026
metadata.scope: Democratic socialism articulated by DSA, including its current democratic socialist republic, social-ownership and abolitionist programme. This is a specific organisation’s doctrinal variant, not all democratic socialism, and not a profile of any incumbent national government. This is a representative interpretation, not a questionnaire submitted by adherents. Numeric neutral means a stated mixed/conditional judgement, including rejection of the premise where explained; it is not a claim of measured empirical equivalence. Modern biological and technology items are conditional interpretive judgements where no exact historical position exists; they must not be read as empirical findings or a representative survey of adherents.
metadata.phrase: A society in which people democratically govern political institutions and productive resources to meet shared needs.

sources.title: Workers Deserve More: DSA Program, live version accessed 4 October 2026
Socialism, especially ownership, Marxist phases and human nature

axes.brief: DSA proposes universal resident suffrage, proportional multiparty elections, a democratic Congress and an executive and judiciary subordinate to it.
axes.counterEvidence: Judicial subordination is genuine counter-evidence to liberal constitutionalism. Q7 is not forced to the democratic pole; multiparty commitments still reject executive autocracy.

answers.rationale: Multiparty electoral accountability is part of the democratic republic.
Expert appointment would contradict popular working-class government.
Suffrage extends even to permanent residents and incarcerated people.
The programme subordinates the executive to Congress.
Replacing the two-party system requires genuine multiparty competition.
Public democratic control includes investigation of government spending.
The programme explicitly subordinates the judiciary to Congress rather than preserving independent judicial supremacy.
Union power does not substitute union leaders for the electorate.
Multiparty democracy cannot depend on incumbent ideological licensing.
Direct popular control is compatible with binding referendums subject to equality.
A sole leader contradicts the proposed democratic Congress.
A subordinate executive must be removable by representative institutions.
Electoral continuity cannot depend on unilateral executive convenience.
Recall can strengthen ordinary people’s control of representatives.
Unaccountable leadership contradicts the programme’s democratic purpose.
A military takeover cannot constitute worker self-government.

axes.brief: DSA’s programme opposes mass incarceration, criminalisation of addiction, police impunity and state intrusion into intimate life.
axes.counterEvidence: Abolitionist aims do not settle every transitional safety mechanism. Court oversight is a limited safeguard, not endorsement of the existing carceral state.

answers.rationale: Addiction should be a health matter, not punishment for personal choice.
Serious-harm investigation and abolitionist criticism of surveillance create a conditional position.
Protected strikes and organising require space for disruptive peaceful protest.
Opposition to oligarchy depends on robust institutional criticism.
Bodily autonomy weighs against paternalistic coercion aimed only at the adult.
Mass police tracking contradicts the programme’s anti-carceral direction.
Preventing road harm is legitimate but routine coercive policing remains contested.
Preventive confinement without an offence conflicts with the anti-carceral presumption.
Intimate and expressive freedom outweighs official moral objection.
Identification-free organising protects movements from state control.
Suspicionless searches reproduce the policing powers the programme seeks to reduce.
Anticipated disorder is too broad a basis for suppressing a gathering.
Warrants limit police intrusion during a transition toward different safety institutions.
Disclosure of misconduct supports accountability against state impunity.
Community self-defence and risks of interpersonal violence require a conditional judgement.
Unreviewed terrorism detention directly contradicts due process and abolitionist commitments.

axes.brief: Multiracial solidarity, anti-discrimination and tribal sovereignty support cultural inclusion without abandoning universal rights.
axes.counterEvidence: Neither racial justice nor Indigenous sovereignty implies that every cultural practice overrides individual freedom.

answers.rationale: A multiracial society should not privilege majority culture in every conflict.
Equal access and inclusion justify cultural accommodation.
Solidarity does not require migrants to surrender customs.
Foreign identity and equal membership are compatible.
Accessibility favours multilingual provision where needed.
Tribal recognition follows respect for Indigenous sovereignty.
Public resources should not be reserved principally for the dominant culture.
Collective identities and common individual rights must constrain each other.
Inclusive services should accommodate diverse observances.
A multiracial working-class identity includes multiple traditions.
Shared organising is valued without forced cultural assimilation.
Local multilingual signage helps people participate equally.
National identity need not take priority over community identity.
Anti-discrimination supports accommodation but universal safety rules remain relevant.
Several cultural ways of life fit multiracial solidarity.
Cultural conformity is not the purpose of integration.

axes.brief: The live programme explicitly calls for legalised migration, amnesty, abolition of caps and quotas, and a citizenship path for permanent residents.
axes.counterEvidence: No contemporary incumbent national government is presented as implementing this programme. Its demands are proposals, not enacted US policy.

answers.rationale: The programme explicitly rejects caps and quotas.
Legalising migration supports movement to improve living conditions.
Admission should not be restricted to employer-selected skills.
Family reunification follows freedom of migration.
Refugees should not face skills or cultural tests.
Amnesty regardless of status is expressly proposed.
Restrictive ceilings conflict with legalised migration.
Public investment should address shortages rather than excluding migrants.
Ending quotas includes avoiding a common rigid family cap.
Employment is a legitimate route within broader free migration.
Sponsorship requirements would exclude the independent movement envisaged.
Graduates should have a settlement path within broadly legalised migration.
Refugee protection is not contingent on numerical ceilings.
Cultural-origin preference conflicts with multiracial equality.
Common social goods should include migrant residents.
Diversity is valued but difference itself need not determine admission priority.

axes.brief: DSA calls for ending foreign wars and bases, cutting the war apparatus and international criminal accountability; resistance to occupation is separately defended.
axes.counterEvidence: The programme defends resistance to occupation, so absolute nonviolence would misrepresent it.

answers.rationale: National advantage is not grounds for foreign war.
Diplomacy is consistent with ending overseas wars.
Funding military superiority conflicts with defunding the war apparatus.
Anticipatory war carries grave escalation risks despite stated imminence.
Defence and resistance can be legitimate while foreign intervention is rejected.
Compulsory militarisation conflicts with dismantling the war machine.
Substantial compromise is preferable to imperial conflict.
Autonomous targeting deepens the military system being opposed.
Defence should replace overseas power projection.
Recognising resistance to occupation precludes renouncing every armed defence.
Closing overseas bases opposes prolonged expeditionary capacity.
Territorial disputes should not trigger chosen wars.
Militarised coercion contradicts the non-interference programme.
Reducing war risk outweighs performances of military resolve.
Escalatory military espionage conflicts with demilitarisation.
Negotiated reductions accord with cutting the war apparatus.

axes.brief: International solidarity and ICC accountability coexist with rejection of coercive US interference and sanctions.
axes.counterEvidence: DSA rejection of military blocs and economic coercion limits how far existing international institutions should command states.

answers.rationale: Anti-imperial self-rule and international legal accountability both matter.
Binding human-rights rules are supported but domination by existing institutions is rejected.
Support for ICC prosecution limits national judicial finality.
Existing military alliances can obstruct the anti-war programme.
A country should be able to leave coercive military arrangements.
ICC accountability expressly includes US officials.
International worker solidarity can outweigh immediate US advantage.
Climate and ecological problems justify shared democratic action.
A common peaceful policy may help but military-bloc discipline is opposed.
Rights-based institutions can legitimately challenge national abuses.
Democratic monetary control matters more than whether authority is national or shared.
Shared resources can advance international social and ecological goals.
International cooperation is preferable to unilateral exclusionary border authority.
Common trade rules are acceptable only when compatible with worker control.
International federation is conditional on democracy rather than required or prohibited.
Collective rights enforcement can help while sanctions and military enforcement can violate non-interference.

axes.brief: DSA explicitly seeks public ownership of major corporations, essential sectors, housing, energy and transport; social ownership must be democratic.
axes.counterEvidence: IEP and SEP distinguish social control from mere bureaucratic nationalisation. Small-scale production is not equated with ownership of commanding industries.

answers.rationale: The programme seeks public control of major corporations beyond a predominantly private economy.
Utilities are explicitly common goods and essential industries.
Democratic ownership has value beyond matching narrow cost metrics.
Public ownership of major corporations reaches competitive sectors.
The programme calls for expanded public hospitals and clinics.
Publicly owned transport is a named programme commitment.
Lower cost alone does not outweigh labour standards and democratic control.
Social control of finance supports a public banking sector during transition.
Privatisation reverses the stated ownership direction.
Publicly owned social housing is explicitly demanded.
Strategic public accountability can matter even if private regulation is feasible.
Natural resources should serve common needs through public control.
Democratic public delivery is preferred to routine private contracting.
Strategic social control outweighs a one-off sale receipt.
Socially necessary services should be repaired rather than automatically sold.
A democratic public broadcaster can reduce commercial concentration.

axes.brief: Opposition to sanctions and global exploitation favours accessible exchange under labour and environmental protections, rather than national corporate privilege.
axes.counterEvidence: The programme is more explicit on sanctions than tariffs; tariff responses are qualified applications of worker solidarity and democratic control.

answers.rationale: Tariffs can defend labour but national firms deserve no automatic privilege.
Openness is useful only within enforceable social and ecological safeguards.
Public purchasing can sustain union jobs and a green transition.
Supplier choice must not bypass labour and environmental obligations.
Essential production capacity can protect communities from corporate dependency.
Unilateral tariff removal depends on worker and development consequences.
Temporary development protection can serve democratic economic restructuring.
Equal access is appropriate only where it does not defeat social control.
Food resilience can justify selective agricultural protection.
Workers should not simply absorb adjustment costs for global capital.
Retaliatory economic warfare conflicts with the opposition to sanctions and blockades.
Equal ordinary product taxes avoid arbitrary national discrimination.
Subsidies can be socially beneficial or unfair, requiring specific assessment.
Increasing dependence is not justified merely by lowering tariffs.
Strategic social ownership can justify rejecting foreign corporate control.
Cross-border communication and services should generally be accessible.

axes.brief: The programme’s jobs guarantee, rent control and public investment imply strong democratic economic direction, with meaningful worker control.
axes.counterEvidence: Democratic planning differs from officials issuing all workplace instructions. Worker autonomy qualifies compulsory targets.

answers.rationale: Social need and worker control should guide major production.
Democratically determined targets may help but rigid compulsion can defeat workplace democracy.
Essential goods should not depend principally on market purchasing power.
The Green New Deal requires deliberate public investment direction.
Community needs and jobs can justify sustaining production beyond market demand.
Affordable essentials support controls against excessive prices.
Small initiatives merit space while strategic production needs public coordination.
Public credit should serve democratically chosen social priorities.
Capital flight cannot be allowed to veto social transformation.
Public green investment deliberately redirects economic development.
Private currency competition would recreate unaccountable financial power.
A living minimum wage is explicitly demanded.
Empowered workers should bargain rather than receive all wages by bureaucratic schedule.
Public finance should serve the democratic development programme.
Universal rent control is explicitly proposed.
Public coordination is needed, qualified by workplace self-government.

axes.brief: Universal material security and aggressive wealth taxation support substantial redistribution during the transition beyond capitalism.
axes.counterEvidence: Post-capitalist social ownership would change the tax base; these answers address explicitly proposed transitional policies rather than inventing permanent wage inequality.

answers.rationale: Material equality requires substantial progressive redistribution.
Concentrated income is a legitimate target of redistributive policy.
Universal security warrants higher contributions from those with resources.
Provision should enable flourishing rather than mere survival.
Progressive taxation shifts burdens toward capacity to pay.
Large private retention should not outrank common material security.
Inheritance transfers can reduce entrenched class advantage.
The programme’s universal social rights contradict arbitrary benefit expiry.
Aggressive wealth taxation is expressly advocated.
Minimal benefits contradict a dignified universal social floor.
Recreation and accessible social life are explicitly public goals.
Improving collective provision takes priority over general tax reduction.
Income supplements can help workers but should not replace employer wage obligations.
Equal marginal rates ignore unequal resources and social obligation.
Land access is valuable but compensated individual redistribution differs from common ownership.
Universal provision extends well beyond a destitution-only test.

axes.brief: A society free of persecution for religion is consistent with secular civil institutions and voluntary religious socialism.
axes.counterEvidence: Religious socialism is part of the movement but provides no basis for state religious authority.

answers.rationale: Equal religious freedom requires publicly accessible civil law.
No creed should bind the whole socialist republic.
Civil decisions require democratic rather than clerical authority.
Privileged state religion conflicts with equal participation.
Comparative teaching respects believers and nonbelievers alike.
Official faith cultivation would violate freedom of belief.
Civilly enacted rules should govern public courts.
Clerical vetoes are incompatible with democratic self-government.
Inclusive government ceremonies should avoid official worship.
Public goods should not be used to promote a particular faith.
Neutral public buildings support equal belonging.
Explicit official recognition privileges a religion beyond a shared day off.
Religious leadership should not itself confer legislative office.
Common charitable rules are preferable to extra creed-based privileges.
Freedom in marriage must be independent of religious approval.
Binding religious family jurisdiction can violate bodily autonomy and equal rights.

axes.brief: The programme directly supports queer liberation, bodily autonomy, gender expression and freedom in family life.
axes.counterEvidence: Current DSA commitments are more specific than older socialist texts, avoiding anachronistic inference where a live programme is available.

answers.rationale: The programme aims to transform restrictive social arrangements.
Inherited custom cannot trump bodily autonomy.
Freedom in childraising includes families beyond a traditional model.
Gender liberation rejects prescribed traditional sex roles.
The programme opposes restrictions on marriage and queer intimacy.
No single family form should receive superior social standing.
Reproductive healthcare and bodily autonomy explicitly include abortion.
Children’s inclusive education should not be suppressed by parental traditionalism.
Queer liberation supports equal parenting recognition.
Gender expression is incompatible with obligatory inherited modesty.
Respect for gender expression supports updated forms of address.
Critical emancipation takes priority over preserving oppressive customs.
Freedom to cross conventional gender roles is explicit.
Urgent rights reforms need not wait for gradual cultural approval.
Inclusive understanding supports teaching diverse gender and sexual identities.
Harmless continuity can be valued voluntarily without compelling preservation.

axes.brief: Worker-led green investment supports beneficial technology but rejects automation controlled solely by bosses and ecological destruction.
axes.counterEvidence: The programme’s criticism of layoffs is counter-evidence to automatic approval of AI productivity gains; green public investment also rules out blanket opposition to development.

answers.rationale: Public benefit must include workers’ control and demonstrable safety.
Significant risks require staged democratic assessment.
Green infrastructure can justify some change but ecological damage remains a serious constraint.
Public healthcare has a duty to establish safety before widespread exposure.
Productivity does not justify mass displacement without workers controlling the transition.
Ecological protection carries strong weight against destructive development.
Food innovation is conditional on environmental evidence and democratic access.
Elective implants warrant careful long-term safety research.
Unproven technological promises should not replace ecological consumption changes.
Poorly understood environmental effects justify delaying irreversible construction.
Personal enhancement needs stronger protection than minimal safety alone.
Equitable public medicine requires evidence across patient groups.
Bodily autonomy and risks of unequal irreversible enhancement point in different directions.
Green stewardship supports ecological safety evidence.
Housing and transit are priorities, but sustainable siting must constrain expansion.
Irreversible harms merit strong precaution rather than corporate optimism.

axes.brief: A powerful democratic Congress and national social guarantees coexist with neighbourhood democracy and tribal sovereignty.
axes.counterEvidence: DSA proposes abolishing the Senate but not all local democracy. National worker and civil rights limit state obstruction.

answers.rationale: Local self-government matters but cannot block national democratic social rights.
The proposed democratic Congress has strong national governing authority.
Self-determination of territories is supported, but not every regional majority settles all rights.
National social guarantees can override regional obstruction.
Regional democratic institutions may vary within national rights.
A single national police hierarchy contradicts decentralised civilian oversight and abolitionist direction.
Keeping local wealth would undermine redistribution to neglected communities.
Common educational equality supports national standards with local participation.
Local fiscal choice is acceptable within a common redistributive framework.
National labour rights protect workers regardless of state.
Neighbourhood democratic power supports local institutional control.
Universal healthcare implies equal national entitlements.
Honouring tribal sovereignty is an express demand.
National rules should prevent tax competition eroding social resources.
Local ecological effects should allow meaningful regional control.
Common emergency coordination can serve need if locally accountable.

axes.brief: DSA explains inequality through institutions, exploitation and discrimination, while socialist scholarship recognises natural capacities and needs.
axes.counterEvidence: Anti-discrimination is a normative commitment, not proof of particular heritability estimates. Mixed answers explicitly avoid deriving biological findings from egalitarian aims.

answers.rationale: The programme emphasises social institutions as powerful shapers of behaviour.

The programme stresses unequal educational opportunity, while individual capacities also vary; these commitments do not establish a majority causal share for either inheritance or upbringing in country IQ differences.
Gender oppression is presented as institutional and socially reproduced.
Recognition of bodily needs and social hardship supports a mixed stress account.
Access to learning and free time expands interests and abilities.
Social insecurity and individual dispositions can both influence risk-taking.
Collective institutions and solidarity cultivate cooperative habits.
Common care can be learned without denying differing innate capacities.
Material conditions affect attention while individual cognitive differences remain possible.
Transforming social relations is expected to change moral habits and reactions.
The programme describes political fear as socially cultivated division.
Temperament can combine personal disposition and social formation.
Bodily preference and cultural standards can both operate.
The programme explains violence through social exclusion and oppressive institutions, supporting a modest structural inference rather than a claim that equal rights prove a biological finding.
Learning and social conditions are preferable to racialised self-control explanations.
The programme identifies sex discrimination and undercompensated care work, challenging an account of the pay gap primarily through differences in productive economic contribution.

review.notes: Read all 240 answers against the current question wording and checked values, rationales, cited source IDs and axis distinctions. Read the live DSA political programme, including the 2026 drafting note. Retained the apparently unusual Democracy07 answer because the programme expressly subordinates the judiciary to Congress; did not replace it with a generic liberal-democratic assumption. Checked public ownership, migrant amnesty, military policy, and inclusive family policies against that scoped programme. Tightened Culture02 and Culture14 to avoid treating anti-discrimination as an empirical causal estimate. All answers remain labelled inferred: these are scoped representative models, not claimed questionnaire responses or empirical measurements of adherents. Review used no target scores or similarity tuning. Similarity audit remains the catalogue coordinator’s separate step.
